svg.text: A knob instead of a switch, and the light has a range

polyline.data-label: to the end of the track

svg.text: to the end of the track
1. Take the button out. The pack, the resistor and the LED stay.
2. Potentiometer: three legs in columns 10, 11 and 12, row c.
3. Purple jumper: column 7 (the LED) to column 10, the end of the track.
4. Black jumper: column 11, the middle leg, to the pack's -.
5. Switch the pack on and turn the knob. The LED brightens and dims.
The middle leg taps the track wherever you turn it, so the resistance is a range, not two states. That is an analogue signal.
A microcontroller reads a voltage like this on an ADC pin, and turns it into a number in your code.
